All 14 queries ran and returned plausible answers. I checked T1 and T4 by hand against the data, and T12 and T13 by hand against `orders.csv`. T10 and T11 gave the expected output. I didn't check the others by hand.

T10 keeps keyword keys in its output (`:db`, `:api`, `:worker`), because `groupBy` keys are keywords.

T1: `| /data/users | filter ~(/active | eq true) | filter ~(at :email | coalesce "" | lower | endsWith "@example.com") | count`
T2: `| /data/users | filter ~(/roles | any ~(lower | eq "admin")) | sort ~(/name | lower) * /name`
T3: `| /data/users | groupBy ~(at :profile | coalesce {} | at :country | coalesce "unknown") * count`
T4: `| /data/users * (at :profile | at :age) | filter ~(ne null) | avg | round 2`
T5: `| sort ~(/number) | filter ~(/state | eq "open") * (/labels * (/name | lower)) | flat | distinct | sort`
T6: `| sort ~([(/comments | desc) /number]) | take 3 * {:number /number :assignee (at :assignee | coalesce null | if (eq null) ~(null) ~(/login))}`
T7: `| filter ~(/state | eq "open") | filter ~(at :assignee | coalesce null | ne null) | groupBy ~(/assignee/login) * count`
T8: `| unionOf /dependencies /devDependencies | entries | filter ~(/1 | startsWith "^") | sort ~(/0) * ([(/0 | keyword) /1] | join "@")`
T9: `| /services | filter ~(at :enabled | eq true) | filter ~(/port | gt 8000) * (/name | lower) | sort | join ","`
T10: `| lines | * split " " | filter ~(/1 | eq "ERROR") * (/2) | groupBy * count`
T11: `| lines | * split " " | * (filter ~(startsWith "ms=")) | filter ~(count | gt 0) * (first | drop 3 | parseJson) | avg | round 1`
T12: `| lines | drop 1 | filter ~(count | gt 0) * (split ",") | filter ~(/5 | lower | eq "shipped") | filter ~(/4 | trim | count | gt 0) * (mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson)) | sum | round 2`
T13: `| lines | drop 1 | filter ~(count | gt 0) * (split ",") | filter ~(/5 | lower | ne "cancelled") | filter ~(/4 | trim | count | gt 0) | groupBy ~(/1) * (* (mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson)) | sum | round 2) | entries * {:customer (/0 | keyword) :total /1} | sort ~(/total | desc) | take 2`
T14: `| ["Banana","apple","Cherry","banana","fig","APPLE","date","kiwi","Fig","elderberry"] * lower | distinct | sort ~([(count | desc) /]) | join "-"`
